leverage.exposure: The recommended move deliberately opens a leveraged position and it must be closed the same morning. Buying Mokwa with the cash on hand puts the balance sharply negative, and a negative balance at matchday start scores zero for the entire matchday — the single largest risk in the game and larger than every other consideration on this page. The unwind is the Conté sale, available instantly at market value, and it should be executed within minutes of the purchase settling rather than left to the lock. There is no open leveraged position right now; this one is a choice, taken because the alternative is leaving a hundred fielded points on the table, and it is safe only if the sale follows immediately.

binding_gap: There is no formation hole. The binding constraint is not shape and not the borrowing floor — it is the unwind ceiling. With the squad at exactly eleven, one purchase permits exactly one sale, so the most that can be spent is cash on hand plus the largest single sale that still leaves a legal eleven. That ceiling is roughly a fifth of nominal spending power, and it is what disqualifies Ginter, Castello, Pavlović and Saibari, every one of whom is affordable against the floor and unaffordable against the unwind.

verdict.detail: One move decides this matchday: raise the standing Mokwa offer before it resolves at 06:27:47Z today, then instantly sell Conté the moment it lands. Mokwa is a straight attacker-for-attacker swap that is worth about a hundred fielded points, and the fitness doubt that three earlier runs carried against him is now dead — he started and scored at Gladbach on 5 September, and the injury item that spooked the ledger has been dated to a preseason friendly in late July. The order is not optional: buy first, then sell. Selling first drops the squad below eleven and costs a flat hundred-point penalty.

sell.reason: Conté, conditional on the Mokwa purchase landing first, by instant sale to Kickbase. This is a rank sale and a funding sale, not a fitness sale — he is fit and carries no flag. Two corrections to the ledger's record on him, in opposite directions. The earlier claim that a ligainsider page projected him in the starting eleven rests on a broken instrument, and a news sweep this run went the other way and called him an unused substitute on matchday two, which is equally false — he scored well that week and cannot have done so from the bench. What is true, from Kickbase's own participation fields, is that he has one start in two matchdays with Lemperle back from suspension. A rotation body in the worst-value slot in the eleven. If the Mokwa auction is lost, this sale must not happen.

movers.reason: No flip clears its cost this run. Every manager ask on the board sits above market value, so the flip mechanism is absent entirely, and cash on hand would not fund one in any case. Rivals in this league are flipping injured and unavailable players for fractions of a percent on the daily tick; that is motion, not points, and it is not worth copying.

fitness.sweep: All eleven squad players are fit and unflagged, verified against dated sources from 5 and 6 September. Neuer, Matsima, Wolf, Gregoritsch, Nusa, Onyeka, Guirassy and ter Horst all started their matchday-two fixtures. Two source rules were established this run and they matter more than any single player. First, the eleven-man grid on a ligainsider club page is a performance-based Top11, not a matchday prediction — that one fact explains a week of contradictions in this ledger, including the grid that benched Mokwa while starting Sirch. Second, and cutting the other way, an external lineup summary does not outrank Kickbase's own participation data; two players were reported as unused substitutes this run when Kickbase's scoring proves they played.
